prompt:
The Jetson Orin cluster runs DeepSeek-V4-Flash with tensor parallelism across four nodes connected by 10Gbit RoCE. Each node is an NVIDIA Jetson Orin with a 275-Sparse-TOPS GPU at 50 watts, which makes memory bandwidth the binding constraint far more often than compute. The serving stack applies fp8 and fp4 quantization to cut memory traffic, speculative decoding to raise inter-token throughput, and expert parallelism to spread the active experts across the node group.

Quantization on this hardware is a trade: the fp8 and fp4 weights halve and quarter the bytes moved for a bandwidth-bound device, but the dequantized values land in bf16, and on consumer-class tensor cores bf16 arithmetic runs at roughly half the rate of fp16. Whether that penalty shows up in the measured step wall depends on how much of the step is compute-bound versus memory-bound, and on where the dequant actually happens in the Marlin kernels the model uses.

The scheduler decides how much work each forward pass can absorb. Speculative decoding at five draft tokens caps the number of scheduled tokens per step, and the server prints a warning when that cap drops below what the configuration otherwise allows. The campaign therefore measures the effect of lifting the batched-token budget instead of trusting the warning either way, and it records the startup KV cache tokens and maximum concurrency before trusting any throughput number.

KV cache sizing interacts with the long-context workload: a 262,144 token maximum context means every concurrent request reserves a large block of key-value storage, and the cache memory is fixed at startup. Raising it toward the GPU memory utilization budget increases the number of concurrent long-context requests the cluster can serve, but it has already OOM'd once at ten gigabytes with larger prompts, so the campaign caps the new value at the known-good ceiling unless a fresh out-of-memory test passes at a higher value.

Speculative decoding turns decode latency into a two-part number. The step wall measures the time between successive target-model outputs, while acceptance measures how many of the draft tokens actually get committed. Both matter: a faster step with much worse acceptance can make the wall-clock inter-token latency look better than it feels. The benchmark therefore reports step wall and acceptance separately and never combines them into a single headline number.

The cluster measures itself through one reusable harness. A benchmark client runs on the head node against the local serving endpoint, the prefix cache counters are scraped before and after so warm-cache flattery cannot fake a time-to-first-token win, and every run is appended to a ledger with its power mode pinned at fifty watts. Configuration arms differ only by their declared override, so the within-run ratios stay trustworthy.

Experts in a mixture-of-experts model are not all active on every token. Expert parallelism shards the expert weights across the nodes and dispatches each token to the experts that need it, trading all-to-all communication for local compute. On a cluster where the network is fast relative to memory bandwidth this can be a clear win, and the campaign traces the communication wall share only if the serving benchmark shows the decode step is communication-bound.

A change that preserves the measured step wall and acceptance is adopted only when it also survives the numerics gate: greedy generation with temperature zero must return identical token ids under the old and new configuration. If tokens diverge, the change is recorded but not auto-adopted, because a throughput win that changes what the model says is a different product decision.

Every adopted or refuted configuration is recorded with its measured delta in the campaign ledger, so a future session inherits the conclusions instead of re-deriving them. The measurement rules caught the campaign out several times when they were not followed literally, so the checklist is treated as non-negotiable: judge decode on step wall and acceptance separately, never trust inter-token latency from few trials, prove the cache is cold, and confirm acceptance claims on natural text rather than random synthetic tokens.

The reference launch config pins the model, the tokenizer mode, the reasoning parser, the four-way tensor parallelism with the master address on the internal network, expert parallelism, chunked prefill, a block size of two hundred fifty six, fp8 delta-scaling MLA key-value cache, prefix caching, a maximum of eight sequences, and five speculative tokens sampled probabilistically. Every arm of the campaign is that line plus exactly one declared override, so the comparison stays apples to apples across the cluster.
